opening_message:
Ticket 1: Eric Woods (employee ID E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E019.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. As full-time, write is within policy (admin would require owning role; Engineer does not own Payroll). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E019 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR says full-time Engineer, Security says contractor with basic security training. Security DB is the authoritative source for employment type and training status, so E019 is a contractor with basic training. Contractors without advanced training max out at read and can never have admin. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.
